title: Excelsoft Technologies Ltd - 544617 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹812 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 30.3% from 40.5% on a ₹85 mn-per-quarter US near-shore team cost booked in other expenses.
summary.overview: Excelsoft reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹812 mn (up 16% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹2,725 mn (down from the ₹3,333 mn stated for FY25, although management described FY26 growth as 17%). Q4 EBITDA fell 13% YoY to ₹246 mn and PAT fell to ₹166 mn from ₹205 mn, as other expenses rose 76% to ₹209 mn on a 30-person US near-shore consultant team hired from January. Management said the cost is a one-off that will lift margins back to about 30-31%, and it flagged a planned UK awarding-body (AQA) announcement and a renewed acquisition push under new CEO Doreswamy Palaniswamy.

segments.name: Educational technology services (ETS)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew about 37% YoY (up ₹117 mn) and share was 54% in Q4 and 56% in FY26. ETS services gross margin is about 56%, per management.

segments.name: Assessment and proctoring solutions (A&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of ₹744 mn, up 18%; share was 29% in Q4 and 27% in FY26. Management did not give a test-volume figure on the call.

segments.name: Learning and student success solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 14% of Q4 revenue and 12% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Learning design and content solutions
segments.commentary: Contributed 3% of Q4 revenue and 5% of FY26 revenue; a new US engagement with an online course content provider was won in the year.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America was 62.7% of Q4 revenue and 64.9% of FY26 revenue. Europe and UK was 25.4% in Q4 and 22.7% in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins to return to the normal range of about 30-31% once the US near-shore team cost is absorbed (said in response to an analyst question).
Management expects to return to organic growth of about 20-25% overall.
The AQA (UK awarding body) engagement is said to have started on the basis of a 1 March LOI; a larger AQA announcement was said to be due within one to two days of the call.
The US near-shore team's gross margin is currently about 30%, and management expects it to move toward roughly 54-56% as other services business is scaled.

Management is pursuing inorganic opportunities, including overseas acquisitions in the US, and says the acquisition strategy is 'intact and in progress', with new CEO Doreswamy Palaniswamy now leading it.
Management plans to reduce capitalised product development over time and expense more of it, and says the ratio of intangible investment to revenue is declining.
capex_capacity: Around 30 professionals hired in January 2026 as consultants for a US near-shore services team, at a cost of about ₹8.5 cr per quarter (about ₹34 cr annualised), expensed in other expenses.
AI R&D team of about 45 people with NVIDIA GPU laptops and data-center GPUs, plus edge compute (NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi) testing.
AI-enabled infrastructure is being built at the network edge and in Excelsoft's own secure data centres rather than relying wholly on public cloud.
Intangible assets capitalised were ₹12.2 cr in FY26, with cumulative book value of about ₹100 cr and annual amortisation of about ₹18 cr.
Three additional senior sales hires in the US, one in the Middle East and one in the UK, plus a few in India; two senior marketing and business development consultants engaged.
demand_pricing: Management said it has not lost a client and that the top 10 clients have an average tenure of about 11 years. Top 5 clients were about 68% of FY26 revenue and top 10 about 78%.
Added 14 new clients in FY26. Pipeline is focused on education, certification, publishing and public sector.

New wins include a multi-year VTCT Skills engagement (about 300,000 vocational and technical exams a year), the Civil Service Commission of the Philippines, and an UK engagement with a large examination body, with rollout over three years. Other UK vocational partners named include AQA, TQUK, VTCT and CQI.
April 2026 revenue was about ₹23 cr against about ₹15 cr in April 2025, which management linked partly to new business from the near-shore team.
Management said handwritten-script digitisation (AI text extraction and e-marking) is a new business line; one customer accounts for about 12 million answer scripts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~₹8.4-8.5 cr quarterly near-shore expense one-off or recurring, and why is it in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the team of about 30 is a fixed cost that will recur at about ₹8.5 cr a quarter but will not grow further. Consultants were used for legal reasons and the cost sits in other expenses because they are not on payroll; lock-ins are in place.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential and margin of the 30-member US team?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is at least 15% above the team's cost. Gross margin is about 30% currently, against about 56% for typical technology services, and is expected to converge as offshore and near-shore work combine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the confirmed order backlog, split between ETS and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the order book, including confirmed and expected, is just over ₹300 cr and executable, of which technology services is about ₹175 cr. It excludes expansion of existing customers and new wins.

qa_highlights.question: How many A&P tests were conducted in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure and said it would announce a break-up of test types (formative, high-stakes, proctored and non-proctored) later.

qa_highlights.question: Who is the new CEO and what will he change?
qa_highlights.answer: Doreswamy Palaniswamy is a Chartered Accountant with about 25 years of experience, including CFO and COO roles and about 13-14 acquisitions. He will set direction, focus on platformisation and acquisitions, and rely on the existing team.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the acquisition process, which has been paused for about six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy is intact. Work was paused until the new CEO reviewed it, and due diligence is being refreshed and is progressing significantly.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the US near-shore team converting into business, and its gross margin is currently about 30% against a company norm of about 56%.

Q4 PAT fell 19% YoY and FY26 EBITDA was flat, while the reported FY26 figures imply a decline in revenue versus FY25 (₹2,725 mn vs ₹3,333 mn), so the reconciliation of the growth figures needs checking.
The AQA announcement and its revenue size were still pending at the time of the call, and management declined to quantify it.
Acquisition timing is uncertain, with spending on diligence and a paused process before the new CEO's review.
Intangible capitalisation (₹12.2 cr in FY26; cumulative ~₹100 cr; amortisation ~₹18 cr a year) will be a recurring D&A and profit-quality item to track.
Concentration risk: top 5 clients are about 68% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and order visibility, but defensive and evasive on specifics: the near-shore cost was framed as a one-off even though it recurs quarterly, and A&P test volumes and AQA size were deferred to future announcements.
key_quotes: That means a direct attributable expense of 85 million in Q4 towards establishing this team is part of other expenses because they were hired as consultants.
This was pretty much one-off where the margin was shrunk because of this expense.
The fact that we have not lost a client but we are able to do more with clients from last year gives us a competitive edge in the marketplace.
So the acquisition strategy is intact and in progress.

adds.what: 30-person US near-shore consultant team hired Jan 2026 (services capacity, cost ~Rs8.5 cr/quarter expensed)

growth.why: Management guides to a return to about 20-25% organic growth (medium term) and 30-31% normalised EBITDA margin in FY27, backed partly by a ~Rs300 cr executable order book, 14 new clients, new UK/US wins and April revenue of Rs23 cr vs Rs15 cr, but no specific capacity numbers or timing were given.

mgmt.note: Doreswamy Palaniswamy is the new CEO and is now leading the acquisition strategy, which management says is intact and in progress; the call did not give a join date.
initiatives: Renewed acquisition push including overseas acquisitions in the US
